title: Dynamic reservation and hosted surge failsafe plan
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Dedicated pools can experience rapid localized surges that either (a) degrade p99 latency for tenants pinned to dedicated capacity, or (b) cause blunt failover to hosted which increases cost and can violate tenant data policies. We need a policy layer that: 1) preserves tenant SLAs on dedicated where possible, 2) admits graceful, budgeted spillover into hosted when safe, and 3) provides circuit-breaker style protections to avoid thrashing or cost storms.

Proposal summary: Implement a lightweight in-orchestrator policy called Dynamic Reservation + Surge Failsafe. Key components:
- Per-tenant "reservation bucket" (token budget) that smooths short bursts via credits. Credits accumulate slowly during idle periods and decay with a tunable half-life during use.
- Reservation decay constant uses exponential decay (half-life default 10 minutes) to allow short spikes without immediate hosted failover.
- Surge-credit bank allows limited hosted egress for tenants when dedicated is saturated. Each tenant has a daily hosted budget; overflow is allowed only if tenant policy permits.
- Two-step fallback: a soft-demotion route to a cheaper, compatible model-variant (same family, quantized) with a short grace hysteresis; if saturation persists beyond a hard threshold (configurable: default 90s sustained 80%+ GPU util and queue depth > 50), trigger controlled hosted spillover.
- Circuit-breaker with backoff windows per-tenant and per-region to avoid thundering herd. Backoff exponentially increases up to 30 minutes.
- Observability: new metrics (tenant_reserved_tokens, tenant_surge_credit, route_demotions, hosted_spill_events) and dashboard for incident debugging.

Design goals & trade-offs:
- Keep runtime decision latency minimal (<2ms added) by computing reservations and thresholds in routing layer, using approximate counters.
- Prefer model-variant demotion over hosted for cost reasons, but only when quality loss is within evaluated bounds (eval harness A/B must pass).
- Accept small increase in control-plane complexity to avoid repeated full-hosted failovers that spike costs.

Success criteria:
- Reduce unplanned hosted_spill_events by 40% in first month for tenants with dedicated pools.
- Maintain p99 token latency uplift <= 60ms when using soft-demotion.
- No tenant exceeds daily hosted budget without explicit PM-approved override.

Docs & artifacts: design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Dynamic+Reservation+Design , perf notes: drive.redwood.ai/r/drive/perf/dyn-reservation/summary, eval harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/212
comments: 2026-02-21 - Kickoff: scoped feature after postmortem on incident 2026-02-19 where a single tenant spike caused unlimited hosted failover. Action: prototype reservation bucket in staging router (Maya).

2026-02-25 - Architecture review: agreed to keep decision path stateless where possible; counters will be approximate (CM Sketch) to avoid cross-process sharding complexity. Liam suggested adding per-region grace windows so multi-region tenants don't oscillate. Action: prototype patch to router's filter chain.

2026-03-02 - Prototype results: staging loadgen showed 55% fewer hosted_spill_events with reservation half-life=10m and surge bank=3% of daily tokens. p95 latency unchanged; p99 increased by ~30ms for demoted requests. Need PM signoff on model-variant quality thresholds.

2026-03-04 - PM feedback (Olivia Park): require explicit tenant opt-in for hosted egress by default; default to model-variant demotion only. Update policy config to respect tenant enterprise flags. Also add UI controls in Console to inspect surge credit and revoke hosted permission.

2026-03-06 - Security review kickoff: security asked for audit traces for any hosted egress even when tenant opted-in (audit event with reason and token bucket snapshot). Added 'hosted_egress_audit' event to plan.

2026-03-08 - Implementation note (Liam): implemented soft-demotion lane using variant compatibility matrix; demotion only allowed if eval delta <= 1.5% on top-1/ROUGE metrics (configurable per-model). Added feature flag router.dynamic_reservation_v1 for staged rollout.

2026-03-09 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/4567 — includes reservation bucket, surge credit accounting, and unit tests for backoff behavior. Loading test harness added in separate PR to evals repo.

2026-03-10 - Testing: ran chaos test with 100 tenants -> targeted tenants with dedicated pools saw drop in abrupt hosted failovers. Observability: dashboard prod-sim/dyn-reservation shows tenant_surge_credit trending down for heavy users. Next: add per-tenant telemetry export to Console and finalize runbook for SRE.
